PACKAGE BEE BOX— SPECIFICATION

Apiaiy Industry Sectional Committee, FAD 3 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Apiary 
Industry Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. 

Beekeeping in modern hives is practiced all over the country wherever suitable flora is available. The main 
object of rearing honey bees is to get honqr jfrom them. Beeswax is also a product as a subsidiary income. The 
bees depend upon the flowers of forest and Agri-horticultural crops. 

It has been proved beyond doubt that cross pollination in Agri-horticultural crops increase the yield many 
fold and the honey bees are very effective cross pollinators. Therefore, the demand for the bee colonies from 
the beekeepers for honey and wax production and from the farmers to effectively cross pollinate their crops 
is increasing day by day. It is not possible to get the colonies everywhere and anywhere as per the requirements 
of the beekeepers and farmers. Therefore, standardization of a simple box to transport the bee colonies from 
one place to another has become a necessity. 

This process of transporting bee colonies with the hives involves heavy expenditure. Secondly, the bee breeder 
or the beekeeper who want to sell their bee colonies cannot afford to sell them alongwith the frames and hives 
every time. Similarly, a beekeeper or an orchard owner who desire to purchase bee colony cannot afford to 
pay for the frames and hives also every time. In order to save unnecessary transport of bee boxes to and fro 
every time it is economical for both the buyer and seller of bee colonies to have a simple and cheap package 
bee box to transport a queen with few thousands of worker bees from one place to another. Such package 
bees are used in making the colonies strong during honey flow season for augmenting the number of colonies 
and also for keeping the bees wherever they are required to effect bee pollination. This standard has been 
drawn up giving due consideration to all these points. 



IS 14136 : 1994 



Indian Standard 
PACKAGE BEE BOX — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes the dimensions and 
other requirements of package bee boxes. 

1.2 These boxes are designed in such a way so as to 
carry only a queen and cluster of honeybees from one 
place to another, providing adequate ventilation, 
food and protection. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary ad- 
juncts to this standard: 

IS No, Title 

399 : 1963 Classification of commercial timbers 
and their zonal distribution (revised) 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

3.1 Package Bee Box 

li is a rectangular box of sbc sides of which two sides 
are fitted with thin bee proof wire gauze and the rest 
of the four sides are covered with wooden planks 
of 12 mm thickness. The joints of the planks are 
nailed together firmly. On the top plank there is a 
round hole to accommodate a tin of feeder and a slit 
to accommodate a queen cage. Funnel is used for 
shaking bees into the transportatipn cage. The funnel 
shall be of 20 cm to 25 cm diameter. 

3.2 Feeder Can 

Can is filled with 50:50 sugar syrup and lid is sealed 
with can sealer. Feeder can is inserted into the hole 
in the top of the cage and rests on a cross bar 
supported at each end to form a 'H' shaped sup- 
port, nailed across the middle of the cage to the cage 
bottom. 

3.3 Queen Cage 

It is a small cage used to confine the queen alongwith 
few workers in the package bee box for her protection 
while on transit and easy to locate while transferring 
the bees to regular hives. After filling the shipping 
cage, the caged queen is hung by a metal tab attached 
near one end of the queen cage which is inserted in a 
spot in the top of the package cage and is bent over 
to secure the queen cage near the feed can. The feed 
can is then dropped into place. 



4 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

4*1 Dimensions 

All dimensions stated in this specification shall be 
regarded as finished dimensions and shall be 
measured after the compilation of finished opera- 
tions such as planning and smi papering. 



4.1.1 Si2e of The 
Cage 



-/-■! 



'ge Bee Boxes and the Queen 



Depending upon the strength of the colony i.e. the 
number of bees alongwith queen to be transported, 
the size of the bees and the climatic condition of the 
locality, the following two sizes can be used. Box of 
smaller size 25 cm X 15 cm x 20cm(Lx Bx H) 
and a slightly bigger size 35 cm x 15 cm x 20 cm. 
These sizes will provide adequate ventilation to the 
bees according to their size and strength. Size of 
Package Bee Boxes will be as follows: 

i) 25 cm X 15 cm X 10cmforbees(v4, ceran^j 

in Southern states 
ii) 35 cm X 15 cm x 20 cm lor bees (A cerana) 

in North hilly race 
iii) 30 cm x^ 15 cm x 22 cm for A meliifera for 

1 kg package bees 

iv) 40 cm X 15 cm X 22cmforAme/ft/crafor 
1*5 kg package bees 

v) 40 cm X I5cmx 26 cm for A, mellifera for 

2 kg package bees. 

4.2 Finish 

The different parts of the package bee box particular- 
ly wooden surfaces shall have a smooth finish with the 
edges trimmed square and smooth. The outer side of 
the wooden planks shall be painted with a suitable 
paint for protection and long lasting of the box. The 
paint shall be non-toxic and shall not have any odour 
disagreeable to the bees. The colour of the paint may 
be of any choice. 

4.3 Joints 

All joints shall be sound and shall withstand normal 
use and transport. Joints of the walls shall be joined 
by slabbed joint firmly. 



!S 14136 : 1994 



4.4 Wire Gauze 

The wire gauze used for the two sides be of the 
galvanized mild steel of 5 wires per cm and shall be 
suitably annexed with side walls by hails. 

4.5 Wood 

Unless specified otherwise the thickness of the 
wooden planks used shall be 12 mm. It shall be of well 
seasoned timber (see IS 399 : 1963), 

5 PACKING 

5.1 The package bee box shall be supplied in a com- 
plete form properly assembled or in separate parts as 
agreed to between the purchaser and the vendor. It 
shall be packed in such a way so as to protect the 
wooden as well as iron parts from damage in transit 
and during storage. 



6 MARKING 

6.1 Each package bee box shall be legibly and in- 
delibly marked with the following: 

a) Name of the part and its size; 

b) Registered trade mark, if any; 

c) Batch or code number; 

d) Name of the manufaaurer; and 

e) Date of manufacture. 

6.2 BIS Certification Marking 

The product may also be marked with BIS Standard 
Mark. 

6.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 
1986 and the Rules and Regulations m.ade there- 
under. The details of conditions under which the 
licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be 
granted to manufacturers or producers may be ob- 
tained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
